SELECTED_INDEX: 7
CONFIDENCE: 0.26
EXPLANATION:  The spectrum is dominated by two very strong C-H stretching bands at 2917 cm⁻¹ and 2981 cm⁻¹ together with a weaker CH stretch at 2820 cm⁻¹, consistent with an aliphatic molecule that contains mostly –CH₂– / –CH₃ groups.  A very intense band at 1057 cm⁻¹ and a second band at 1337 cm⁻¹ form the characteristic pair of νs(SO₂) and νas(SO₂) vibrations of a sulfone or sulfonamide group (rule GFQ-022).  
Two medium bands at 927 cm⁻¹ and 943 cm⁻¹ fall in the typical region for NH₂ wagging modes (rule GFQ-002), indicating the presence of primary amine groups.  
Candidate 7, NCCSS(=O)(=O)CCN, contains  • an SO₂ group (accounting for 1057 and 1337 cm⁻¹)  • two terminal –NH₂ groups (explaining the 927/943 cm⁻¹ doublet)  • several aliphatic –CH₂– units (matching the three C-H stretching bands and the 1493/1251 cm⁻¹ CH₂ deformation modes).  
It also lacks C=O or aromatic bonds, consistent with the absence of any bands in the 1600–1750 cm⁻¹ region.  None of the other candidates simultaneously provide an SO₂ group without a carbonyl band and two NH₂ groups needed for the observed features, so candidate 7 gives the best overall match.
